decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 0% to 0.25%. The vote was 9-1. Dissenting: Eric S. Rosengren.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in October indicates that economic activity is expanding at a moderate pace.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in September generally suggests that economic activity has continued to expand at a moderate pa…”

changes.quote: Labor market conditions have shown further improvement; the unemployment rate has declined but remains elevated.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Indicators of labor market conditions have shown some further improvement, but the unemployment rate remains elevated.”

changes.quote: Household spending and business fixed investment advanced, while the recovery in the housing sector slowed somewhat in recent months.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Available data suggest that household spending and business fixed investment advanced, while the recovery in the housing sector slowed somewhat in recent months…”

changes.quote: Fiscal policy is restraining economic growth, although the extent of restraint may be diminishing.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Fiscal policy is restraining economic growth.”

changes.quote: Inflation has been running below the Committee's longer-run objective, but longer-term inflation expectations have remained stable.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Apart from fluctuations due to changes in energy prices, inflation has been running below the Committee's longer-run objective, but longer-term inflation expect…”

changes.quote: The Committee sees the risks to the outlook for the economy and the labor market as having become more nearly balanced.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The Committee sees the downside risks to the outlook for the economy and the labor market as having diminished, on net, since last fall.”

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee also reaffirmed its expectation that the current exceptionally low target range for the federal funds rate of 0 to 1/4 percent will be appropriate at least as long as the unemployment rate remains above 6-1/2 percent, inflation between one and two years ahead is projected to be no more than a half percentage point above the Committee's 2 percent longer-run goal, and longer-term inflation expectations continue to be well anchored.
In light of the cumulative progress toward maximum employment and the improvement in the outlook for labor market conditions, the Committee decided to modestly reduce the pace of its asset purchases.

The Committee's sizable and still-increasing holdings of longer-term securities should maintain downward pressure on longer-term interest rates, support mortgage markets, and help to make broader financial conditions more accommodative, which in turn should promote a stronger economic recovery and help to ensure that inflation, over time, is at the rate most consistent with the Committee's dual mandate.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 11.88% APR costs about $49.50 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.89% and moved +4 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 4.46% would rise by about $7.12 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 6.9%, and employers added an average of 224k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.2% over the past year (November 2013); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.5%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 3.4% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -2 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.13% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is dovish (leaning toward lower rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 84%, cut 15%, hike 1%.
